relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - new axis of gating not covered by existing predicates (requiresCapellaRole/incompatibleWithCredentialType/requiresUiMode all describe identity, credential, or UI-mode gates; this is about which client/access surface can execute the statement family at all). Modeled on the shape of incompatibleWithCredentialType.
relations.evidence: Couchbase Transactions are not supported via the Couchbase Capella Query tab or the Data API (Query Service passthrough). The Query Service requires that the whole transaction must be executed by a single node, and there is currently no way for the Query tab or the Data API to enforce this.

notable_absence.finding: The 'Permissions' section names no specific privilege at all - it only says generically 'users must have the relevant cluster access privileges, with permissions on the relevant buckets, scopes and collections' and points to the general Manage Cluster Access Credentials page, unlike the DML statement pages in this batch (update.md, upsert.md) which name exact Basic/Advanced privileges per statement. The transaction-statement family sits outside the credential-type-keyed privilege model this round otherwise confirmed extends cleanly to collections/UDFs/sequences.

cross_component_finding: This overview page introduces a third gating axis beyond RBAC/edition/deployment/UI-mode already in the registry: an access-surface gate (incompatibleWithAccessSurface) - the statement family works via cbq shell and SDKs but is explicitly excluded from the Capella Query tab and the Data API because 'the whole transaction must be executed by a single node, and there is currently no way for the Query tab or the Data API to enforce this.' This same shape recurs verbatim in this batch's using-ai.md (USING AI is also excluded from the Query tab, plus Couchbase Shell/cbsh) - two independent statements in this batch hit the identical constraint, suggesting incompatibleWithAccessSurface is a real recurring axis, not a one-off.
cross_product_finding: Per task brief: checked whether this page's own content links or relates to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction). It does not name or link to it directly, but it does say 'Some Couchbase SDKs provide APIs to support Couchbase transactions. For more information, see [Transactions](../../../server/current/learn/data/transactions.md) in the Server documentation' - a link to server/'s transaction overview, not to any SDK-specific page, and the SDK feature name is never mentioned. Flagging as an open question per the task brief: this SQL++ statement family and the Java SDK's distributed ACID transactions are plausibly the same underlying server-side mechanism exposed via two different client surfaces (cbq shell/SDK query-mode vs. SDK transaction lambda), but no relation is asserted since this page gives no explicit textual cross-reference to the SDK feature.
